zh-CN.The analog style keeps the traditional h: The analog style keeps the traditional hour and minute hand layout, which some people read faster than digital numerals, especially for quick relative judgments like how much time is left before an hour mark.
zh-CN.The minimalist style strips the display: The minimalist style strips the display down to the essential digits with little decoration. This style suits situations where the clock needs to blend into a workspace, like a coding setup or a studio desk, without pulling attention away from other work.

zh-CN.The binary clock style encodes the time: The binary clock style encodes the time in binary digits rather than standard numerals. zh-CN.The neon glow style uses a bright accent: The neon glow style uses a bright accent treatment against a dark background, which suits dim rooms, desk setups with ambient lighting, or anyone who wants the clock to double as a small decorative element.
zh-CN.Flip Clock For A Retro Feel: Flip Clock For A Retro Feel
zh-CN.The flip clock style recreates the look: The flip clock style recreates the look of a mechanical flip-number clock. It has a strong retro aesthetic and works well for users who want a nostalgic display without giving up the underlying NTP accuracy.

zh-CN.Every clock style can be paired with cus: Every clock style can be paired with custom accent colors and a multi-color display option, and night mode reduces brightness for bedroom or low-light use. The keep-screen-on option matters most here, since a precision clock used as a desk display or bedside reference needs to stay visible without the screen dimming or locking.
zh-CN.Choosing A Style For Your Use Case: Choosing A Style For Your Use Case
